75af24a46374.title: Dropping an overlength replay leaves its whoosh cue behind

79e94e61b5a9.title: Proof-mode ledger is evidence without an integrity boundary
79e94e61b5a9.observation: capture_cli.py describes itself as the truthfulness layer whose replay and measured claims come from recorded artifacts. It hashes files that callers explicitly record, but the displayed shell_line is accepted directly from the caller, and save_ledger()/load_ledger() simply serialize and deserialize ordinary JSON. Nothing in this module binds argv, terminal events, shell_line, measurements, and referenced file hashes into one identity that a downstream renderer can verify before replay.

Keep human-readable JSON, but make tampering or accidental post-capture edits detectable rather than trusted by convention.

71d8f01ef635.title: Recovered media checkpoints bypass their contract validator
71d8f01ef635.observation: When response.json omits a request or is absent, Phase B reconstructs pointers with recovered_media and adds them to idx['media']. It then calls validate_response_media on the unchanged response object, not on the augmented index or a rebuilt response. The recovered entries therefore never reach checkpoint_problems, contract matching, deterministic-filename checks, sharing checks, dimension checks, or duplicate-file detection. pointer_from_checkpoint admits any object marked verified that has only request_id, drive.file_id, and image.sha256. Later, the fetch loop reads the unvalidated recovered pointer from idx and can pin it. This is the exact recovery mode made important by the August 12 critical finalizer-no-artifact alarm.
71d8f01ef635.proposal: Validate each checkpoint before converting it, using the requested date, active bundle identity, request id, prompt, and request kind, then validate a single merged response view so recovered and explicit pointers receive identical cross-entry checks. Refuse any recovered entry that fails and send the shot to the existing self-fill path. Replace the current source-order test with a behavioral test that plants a verified-looking checkpoint with the wrong schema, date, bundle, filename, sharing, and dimensions and proves Phase B refuses it.

1207ec562569.title: Active gated engines have no adoption deadline
1207ec562569.observation: The engine-honesty test correctly rejects an active ungated engine with no consumer and requires decision dates for experimental engines, but it exempts every gated active engine from both rules. Extend the honesty test so consumerless gated engines must carry that lifecycle metadata and so an expired decision date fails. 66d90578bc9b.title: Renderer randomness is not reproducible or attributable
66d90578bc9b.observation: The same package is not a reproducible render. Reddit randomly chooses a gameplay file and seek point; explainer randomly chooses gameplay, a motion window, and a seek; the retained text-card renderer does the same. None accepts or records a render seed. A rerun after a showrunner block can therefore change background footage independently of the intended repair, making A/B diagnosis, regression reproduction, and audit comparison ambiguous.
66d90578bc9b.proposal: Define a shared render-context contract carrying a deterministic seed derived from package identity plus an explicit attempt number. Route all renderer choices through a local seeded RNG, record the seed and chosen asset/time ranges in a versioned audit manifest, and let repairs increment the attempt deliberately. Add cross-renderer tests proving identical package+attempt inputs produce identical plans while a new attempt changes only declared stochastic choices.

None of the three build entry points accepts a seed or RNG, and their audit sidecars do not record one.

f6aa3e1f1c66.title: Test the existing superlative doctrine against the finance-heavy explainer queue

Require at least 25 mature uploads in the treatment; primary metric median average-view percentage, guardrails editorial-block rate, factual-correction rate, and short-slate days. d79703f6f53b.title: The frozen exchange identity omits scripts and takeover briefs
d79703f6f53b.observation: Phase A freezes a running worker's assignment by comparing ask_fingerprint(bundle) with BUNDLE_ID, but the fingerprint hashes only the date, registry fields, and media-request identifiers/prompts/filenames. The same bundle is also the authoritative punch-up work order and may contain whole-channel authoring briefs. A rerun after STARTED.json can therefore change package scripts, shot phrases, authoring_request, or authoring_requests while producing the same identity; Phase A calls that ask unchanged and rewrites bundle.json underneath workers already acting on the prior editorial assignment.
d79703f6f53b.proposal: Make the fingerprint cover a canonical, versioned representation of every actionable input: each package's slug, script and protected shot fields; every per-channel authoring brief; media requests; and the frozen contract. Exclude only explicitly cosmetic/generated fields. Add tests proving that package-script, shot-phrase, target/mix, and other-channel brief changes move the identity after a heartbeat, while ordering and diagnostic media-health changes do not; Phase A must refuse an undeclared mid-flight rewrite.

5a7b4694a767.title: Phase B exits green after losing package or audit writes
5a7b4694a767.observation: Phase B catches each package persistence failure, prints a warning, and continues. It then catches every phase_b_report.json write failure and silently discards the exception before returning zero. Its module contract says exit zero means ready to render, so the workflow can advance with stale packages, lost verified media or punch-up edits, and no audit record while the phase itself reports success.
5a7b4694a767.proposal: Track every intended package write and require all of them plus phase_b_report.json to commit successfully before returning zero or printing ready to render. Return nonzero with the failed paths when any write fails, preserve atomic_write_json, and add fault-injection tests for one package failure, report failure, and the all-success case. This changes publication truthfulness only; editorial acceptance remains exactly as registered.

ee3bb63e4024.title: Authored-shot checkpoints cannot recover a missing response pointer
ee3bb63e4024.observation: The checkpoint protocol defines authored_shot records as durable shared memory and recovered_media walks every verified checkpoint, including authored-shot ids. Phase B inserts all recovered pointers into idx.media, but its normal media loop consumes only bundle.requests, while cover_authored reads only media embedded on response-authored shots. A verified authored-shot checkpoint whose finalizer response omits the matching shot.media pointer is therefore recovered into a map no consumer reads and the shot falls to stock self-fill or remains bare.
ee3bb63e4024.proposal: Make recovery type-aware: return bundle-request pointers separately from authored-shot pointers keyed by package slug and shot index, validate the latter with request_kind=authored_shot and package/shot identity, then attach them to promoted or already-promoted authored packages before cover_authored. Add an end-to-end test with a valid authored-shot checkpoint, a promoted package, and a response that omits shot.media; require the verified image to win without regeneration or stock fallback, plus stale-identity and wrong-package refusal cases.

589a78eabb84.title: Trending takeover has two serialized sources of truth
589a78eabb84.observation: A takeover bundle publishes the trending brief both as authoring_request and as authoring_requests.trending. The singular field is retained as a compatibility alias while the per-channel map is described as the whole signal. Because both copies are ordinary JSON, a partial writer, manual repair, or future producer change can leave different targets, mixes, or instructions; Phase B still reads the singular alias for its target fallback while workers are directed to read the plural map.
589a78eabb84.proposal: Version the bundle contract around one per-channel authoring_requests map and give every consumer a shared accessor. During a bounded migration, accept the singular alias only when it is byte-for-byte equivalent to authoring_requests.trending and fail closed on disagreement; instrument legacy reads, migrate tests and docs, then remove the alias. The canonical accessor should also be part of the expanded ask fingerprint so one authority determines both identity and execution.

5b8318ee7172.title: Pinned image URLs certify themselves as on-topic
5b8318ee7172.observation: When judge_package receives a shot that already has image_url but no separate candidate record, it invents candidate title and query from that same shot. judge_shot then measures the shot phrase against those copied fields, so an unrelated URL earns full semantic overlap; absent dimensions are also awarded the resolution component. The exchange therefore suppresses AI requests for media it has not actually verified as relevant.

Add an adversarial test proving an unrelated URL cannot become strong merely because its shot has a phrase and query.

ab128687aaf7.title: Entity title filtering accepts substring lookalikes
ab128687aaf7.observation: The media prefilter says it requires the entity's final distinctive word in an article title, but implements that requirement as a raw substring. A search for Elon Musk therefore keeps titles about Muskox or Muskrat, allowing an explicitly wrong subject into the scored candidate set.
ab128687aaf7.proposal: Compare the required entity word against normalized whole title tokens (preserving apostrophe and hyphen handling) rather than a substring, and add table-driven cases for Musk/Muskox, Ann/annual, possessives, and punctuation so recall for real surname headlines remains intact.

Calling _prefilter with entity='Elon Musk' keeps Candidate titles 'Muskox herd expands' and 'Muskrat population grows' as well as 'Musk announces launch'; tests/test_media_funnel_cache.py has no boundary-disambiguation fixture.

86ad3ba9d045.title: Experiment conclusions bypass their age and sample floor
86ad3ba9d045.observation: The experiment register advertises that early conclusions are structurally impossible and implements readout_ready with both day and sample thresholds, but conclude never calls it. Any caller holding an experiment dict can immediately persist adopted, reverted, or inconclusive with zero samples, bypassing the register's central safety property.
86ad3ba9d045.proposal: Make conclude reload the canonical experiment, require running/readout_due status, call readout_ready using the persisted sample count and conclusion time, and refuse with the exact readiness reason unless both floors pass. Add tests that direct conclusions at day zero and with zero samples cannot mutate the register, plus a positive test after both floors pass.

d65eddf69fba.title: Authoritative state cannot distinguish corruption from absence
d65eddf69fba.observation: The shared JSON reader returns the caller's empty default for both a missing file and any parse/read failure. That policy is acceptable for expendable caches but unsafe for authoritative posted ledgers: a corrupt dedupe log becomes an empty log, and upload code proceeds as if nothing has shipped. The module header itself identifies corrupt posted state as duplicate-upload risk, yet the read API erases the distinction.
d65eddf69fba.proposal: Separate optional cache reads from authoritative-state reads. Give authoritative ledgers a typed/schema-checked loader that fails closed on corruption, preserves the bad bytes, and can recover from a verified backup or git copy before publishing; keep default-on-error only for explicitly expendable caches. Migrate posting and permission ledgers by risk, and test missing, corrupt, wrong-shape, and recoverable states independently.

aaeb12de3ebd.title: Restore explainer delivery before interpreting its topic test

8bb141fe6f49.title: Explainer fact QA ignores unsupported small integers
8bb141fe6f49.observation: The explainer validator says every spoken number must trace to the attached fact table, but an unmatched token is reported only when it contains a decimal point or is at least 1,000. Unsupported counts, ranks, percentages, ages, and durations from 0 through 999 therefore pass the final package QA despite the stated factual contract.
8bb141fe6f49.proposal: Validate every spoken numeric token against normalized fact values, with explicit typed exemptions for genuine period labels rather than a magnitude shortcut. Add adversarial tests for unsupported 12, 99, and 999 values, plus positive coverage for supported small values and legitimate years, so strengthening the check does not reject sourced narration.

3445b0aecae4.title: Failed Claude processes can return successful Third authoring
3445b0aecae4.observation: Third's Claude wrapper only treats a nonzero process exit as failure when the output matches its usage-limit regex. If a failed CLI invocation emitted a complete or embedded JSON object before exiting, the wrapper returns that object as a successful brain answer, so partial or stale output can drive ranking, scene judgment, or metadata while health accounting reports success.
3445b0aecae4.proposal: Require returncode zero before accepting any JSON from Claude. On every other exit, preserve the usage-limit breaker when applicable and otherwise raise a diagnostic containing bounded stderr/stdout; then add mocked coverage for nonzero-with-valid-JSON, nonzero-with-limit-text, and zero-with-valid-JSON so callers reliably fall back and count the failure.

With subprocess.run mocked to return returncode=1, stdout containing a JSON title of partial, and stderr='fatal transport error', _call_claude returns that parsed object. The Third tests have no assertion for this process-result contract.

5171aa14cc8d.title: Legacy explainer publish writes packages before QA passes
5171aa14cc8d.observation: The legacy data-learning entrypoint advertises --publish as a direct route into the daily production package directory, but it serializes each package before acting on qa.validate errors. QA failures remain in the live slate, and the command still exits zero unless the operator separately remembered --strict, so the gate can be visibly red while downstream rendering sees the rejected artifact.

Add an integration test proving a failed package creates no file under state/trending_packages and makes a publish invocation return nonzero without an extra flag.

347e2440278c.title: Split Third attempts from the authoritative posted ledger
347e2440278c.observation: Third uses one posted dictionary as the durable home for three different lifecycle states: confirmed uploads, rejected blocklist entries, and in-flight upload claims. Every reader must rediscover which entries are real posts through key prefixes and flags, while reporting consequently shows 327 attempts, 188 posts, and 139 rejected-or-pending records. This overloaded projection is both dedupe-critical state and analytics input, so a new writer or forgotten filter can mistake a rejection for a post or a pending claim for a completed upload.
347e2440278c.proposal: Move Third to an append-only, typed attempt ledger with explicit discovered, rejected, upload_claimed, uploaded, and reconciled events, then derive a schema-checked posted projection used only for dedupe and channel counts. Migrate readers behind one shared projection API, preserve every rejection and pending claim during conversion, and add invariant tests that only uploaded events count as posts while all terminal source keys remain blocked from reuse.

2127c6395c2c.title: Challenge Third's oversized chaos bucket with proven alternatives

That bypasses the package workflow_run route's Phase B artifact check, so rendering can begin before ChatGPT's media and editorial response is applied. Require every non-rescue entry into daily.yml, including workflow_dispatch, to validate today's successful Phase B report before rendering. Preserve an explicitly identified rescue route for operators, and add an executable workflow test proving a package merge cannot reach Daily before Phase B succeeds.

03ed6ae9f195.title: The full unit gate discards unittest failures
03ed6ae9f195.observation: The auto-merge job runs the full tests/ suite as `python -m unittest ... 2>&1 | tail -40` without enabling pipefail or checking PIPESTATUS. Bash therefore returns tail's zero status when unittest fails, the following steps continue, and the automerge job may squash-merge a branch whose unit suite is red. Replacing unittest with a process that exits 7 reproduces a pipeline status of zero under the same command shape.
03ed6ae9f195.proposal: Enable pipefail for the step or capture the unittest output and explicitly propagate the test process status before printing its tail. Add a workflow-contract test that executes a deliberately failing producer through the exact reporting wrapper and requires the wrapper to return nonzero, so future log-format changes cannot reopen the bypass.
